domain: A. Identity and access for AI services and agents
title: Distinct identity for every AI service and agent
objective: Every AI component that calls a model, reads customer data or takes an action runs under its own non-human identity with a named owner, so its access can be scoped, reviewed and revoked without touching anything else.
how_to_verify: List every identity used by AI workloads. Each maps to exactly one use case and one owner. No AI workload authenticates with a human account or a shared integration account. Disable one AI identity in a test environment and confirm only that use case stops.

domain: A. Identity and access for AI services and agents
title: Least-privilege access from AI to customer data
objective: An AI identity can reach only the objects, records and fields its approved use case needs, and is read-only unless write access was explicitly approved.
how_to_verify: Compare the permissions granted to each AI identity with the approved data scope. Using the AI identity in test, try to read a field outside the scope. The platform, not the prompt, must deny it. Keep the last access-review record.

domain: A. Identity and access for AI services and agents
title: Agent tools, delegated permissions and human confirmation
objective: An AI agent can call only tools on an approved list, can never do more than the person it acts for is allowed to do, and needs a human to confirm high-impact actions.
how_to_verify: The tool list in configuration matches the approval record. Ask the agent to perform an action that is not allowlisted; the tool layer refuses it and logs the attempt. A high-impact action creates a confirmation request instead of executing. An agent session for a low-privilege user cannot return records that user cannot see. Every MCP server an agent can reach is on the approved list, and a token issued for one server is rejected by another.

domain: A. Identity and access for AI services and agents
title: Administrative access to AI platforms and AI configuration
objective: Administration of model settings, system prompts, retrieval indexes, the AI gateway and model-serving clusters is limited to named people using single sign-on, multi-factor authentication and short-lived elevation, and every change is reviewed and logged.
how_to_verify: List administrators of each AI platform; every one is a named person with MFA enforced. Pick the last change to a system prompt or tool definition and show its review record. No shared or local admin account is in daily use.

domain: B. Secrets and model-provider keys
title: Model-provider credentials stay in a secrets manager
objective: API keys and tokens for model providers, vector databases and AI SaaS tools never appear in source code, container images, notebooks, prompts, client-side code or CRM configuration tables; workloads fetch them at runtime with their own identity.
how_to_verify: A secret-scanning report across repositories and images shows no live AI credentials. Front-end bundles and mobile builds contain no provider keys. The Kubernetes API server has an encryption configuration for Secrets.

domain: B. Secrets and model-provider keys
title: Key scoping, usage limits, rotation and revocation
objective: Each provider credential belongs to one use case and one environment, has usage and spending limits, is rotated on a defined schedule, and can be revoked and replaced quickly.
how_to_verify: The key inventory matches what the provider console shows; there are no unowned keys. Usage or spend alerts are configured for each production key. A tabletop or test shows a key can be revoked and replaced; record how long it took.

domain: C. Network egress control
title: Default-deny egress for AI workloads
objective: AI workloads can reach only approved destinations (named model endpoints and the internal services they need); all other outbound traffic is blocked.
how_to_verify: From a pod in an AI namespace, a request to an unapproved host fails and a request to an approved endpoint succeeds. Every AI namespace has a default-deny egress policy. The network plugin is documented as enforcing egress policy.

domain: C. Network egress control
title: Central AI gateway and detection of unapproved AI services
objective: Production calls to external models pass through one controlled path (AI gateway, API gateway or forward proxy) that authenticates callers, applies data rules, limits rates and logs; use of AI services that are not in the inventory is detected.
how_to_verify: Firewall or egress rules show that only the gateway can reach model-provider endpoints. A dated report of AI-service domains seen in DNS or proxy logs is reconciled against the inventory.

domain: D. Kubernetes isolation for model serving
title: Isolated namespaces and hardened pods for AI workloads
objective: Model serving, retrieval and agent workloads run in dedicated namespaces (or clusters) with restricted pod security, so a compromised AI component cannot reach other workloads or the node.
how_to_verify: `kubectl get ns --show-labels` shows the enforce label on every AI namespace. Deploying a privileged test pod into an AI namespace is rejected. The list of documented exceptions matches what is running.

domain: D. Kubernetes isolation for model serving
title: Admission policy, labels and resource limits for AI workloads
objective: Policies enforced at admission ensure AI workloads come from approved registries, are signed, declare resource limits (including GPUs), and carry labels that link them to the governance inventory.
how_to_verify: Deploying an unlabelled or unsigned image into an AI namespace is rejected. Every running AI workload carries a `use-case-id` that exists in the inventory. ResourceQuotas exist for each AI namespace.

domain: D. Kubernetes isolation for model serving
title: Separate environments and no unapproved production data in AI testing
objective: Experiments, prompt development and evaluations do not use production customer data unless that use is approved, minimized and protected to production standard.
how_to_verify: An inventory of data held in non-production AI environments, with masking status. A sample check of non-production stores finds no unmasked customer extracts without an approval record.

domain: E. Supply chain for models and containers
title: Model inventory, approved sources and integrity
objective: Every model in use (hosted API model, open-weight model, fine-tuned model, embedding model) is recorded with source, version, license, owner and integrity information, and comes from an approved source.
how_to_verify: Inventory entries match what actually runs (gateway logs, model registry, images). The hash of a deployed model file matches the approved record. No workload downloads models from the internet at start-up.

domain: E. Supply chain for models and containers
title: Container images and AI dependencies are scanned, signed and verified
objective: Images and libraries for AI workloads are built from trusted bases, pinned, scanned, signed in the pipeline and verified at admission, with a software bill of materials (SBOM) for each image.
how_to_verify: Each deployed AI image has an SBOM and a current scan with no unaccepted critical findings. An unsigned image is rejected at admission. Each MCP server, plugin or agent framework in use has an approved, pinned version.

domain: E. Supply chain for models and containers
title: Due diligence and contract terms for external AI services
objective: Before customer data is sent to an external AI service, the provider's terms on data use, training, retention, location, sub-processors and security are reviewed and recorded, and acceptable terms are in the contract.
how_to_verify: Each external AI service in the inventory has a dated due-diligence record and a contract reference. The approved tier and account match what is in use.

domain: F. Logging and monitoring with privacy
title: AI interaction audit logging with data minimization
objective: For every AI request the organization can reconstruct who or what asked, which model and version answered, which data and tools were used, and what action followed, without turning logs into a second, uncontrolled copy of customer data.
how_to_verify: Reconstruct one sample AI transaction end to end from the logs. Search the logs for a synthetic test value (for example a fake account number); it does not appear in clear text. Retention settings match the documented policy.

domain: F. Logging and monitoring with privacy
title: Security monitoring for AI misuse
objective: Alerts fire on signs that an AI component is being abused or is misbehaving, and they reach the incident process.
how_to_verify: Trigger each detection with a simulated event in test; the alert reaches the on-call person. The detection list is reviewed when a new use case is approved.

domain: F. Logging and monitoring with privacy
title: Signals for quality and behavior change
objective: The platform records the signals the governance process needs to see when an AI system's behavior changes: model version changes, results of repeat evaluations, user corrections and overrides, and complaints linked to AI output.
how_to_verify: Evaluation results exist for the current model version and the last change. Override and complaint data are available to the owner and reviewed at the periodic gate.

domain: G. Data protection when connecting AI to CRM and customer data
title: Classify customer data before AI gets access
objective: Every object and field an AI use case wants is classified, and each class has a written rule for which kind of AI service may receive it.
how_to_verify: Each AI use case has a data map with a class for every field it uses. The rule matrix is approved and dated.

domain: G. Data protection when connecting AI to CRM and customer data
title: Minimize, mask and filter data going to and coming from models
objective: A model receives only the data the task needs; sensitive values are masked, tokenized or removed before they reach a model or index, and outputs are filtered before they are shown or stored.
how_to_verify: Inspect a sample of requests at the gateway; only allowlisted fields are present. Send a test record containing synthetic sensitive values; they are masked before the model call and do not appear in the output.

domain: G. Data protection when connecting AI to CRM and customer data
title: Permission-aware retrieval and protected AI data stores
objective: Retrieval indexes, vector stores, caches, conversation histories and fine-tuning sets built from customer data enforce the same access rules as the source system, are encrypted, and are listed as customer-data stores.
how_to_verify: Two test users with different CRM visibility ask the same question; each receives only what they may see. Encryption at rest is enabled for each AI data store. Each store appears in the data inventory with an owner and retention rule. Memory written in one customer's session is not visible in another customer's session.

domain: G. Data protection when connecting AI to CRM and customer data
title: Customer and external content is untrusted input
objective: Text that comes from customers or outside parties (emails, chats, tickets, web forms, documents, call transcripts) is handled as untrusted when an AI system reads it, and model output is validated before it triggers an action, is written to a record or is rendered in a user interface.
how_to_verify: The injection test suite was run on the current version and the results were reviewed at the approval gate. A test message containing an instruction to export data or change an account does not lead to that action.

domain: G. Data protection when connecting AI to CRM and customer data
title: Controlled write-back to customer records
objective: Changes an AI system makes to customer records are attributable to the AI identity and use case, validated, limited in volume, and reversible.
how_to_verify: The audit trail shows the AI identity on a sample of AI changes. A rollback test restores a set of AI-changed records. An attempted bulk update above the limit is blocked.

domain: G. Data protection when connecting AI to CRM and customer data
title: Retention and deletion across AI copies of data
objective: Copies of customer data inside AI systems (logs, caches, indexes, conversation histories, evaluation sets and provider-side storage) follow the retention schedule of the source data, and deletion requests reach them.
how_to_verify: For a deleted test customer, search all AI stores; no copies remain beyond the retention rule. Expiry settings match the documented schedule.

domain: G. Data protection when connecting AI to CRM and customer data
title: Safe fallback and a tested kill switch
objective: The business process keeps working when an AI service fails, is rate-limited or is switched off on purpose, and the switch that turns each AI use case off is tested.
how_to_verify: A test turns the use case off and on; the manual path works and the time taken is recorded. The switch owner is named in the RACI (`governance/ROLES_RACI.md`).
